name: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. The full paper documents search/click WebShop actions and 11 browser actions in WebArena, while the overall benchmark also covers non-web domains.
summary: Introduces AgentBoard, a multiturn agent evaluation framework with intermediate progress metrics and analysis tools. Its broader task suite includes WebShop and WebArena interactions with stepwise progress measurements.

name: WebSuite: Systematically Evaluating Why Web Agents Fail
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: WebSuite organizes browser operations into an action taxonomy and tests both isolated controls and complete workflows. Its diagnostic tasks attribute failures to specific actions, enabling comparison of text-based and multimodal web agents.

name: Deep Research Bench: Evaluating AI Web Research Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces Deep Research Bench, 89 multi-step web research tasks and a frozen collection of scraped pages for evaluating search agents and their traces over time.

name: OSWorld-Human: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: OSWorld-Human adds human-determined trajectories to OSWorld to evaluate the efficiency of desktop computer-use agents. The study compares 16 agents and analyzes model-call latency, changes in step duration during task execution, and excess action steps.

name: Measuring Harmfulness of Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The misuse tasks are evaluated in a sandbox.
summary: Introduces CUAHarm, 104 computer-use misuse tasks in a sandbox with verifiable rewards, and studies whether language models can monitor unsafe agent actions.

name: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: FineState-Bench evaluates fine-grained GUI perception and control across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces. Its Visual Diagnostic Assistant separates perception and localization contributions in controlled interaction experiments.

name: You Don't Know Until You Click:Automated GUI Testing for Production-Ready Software Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: RealDevWorld evaluates generated software repositories with 194 development tasks and AppEvalPilot, an agent judge that operates the resulting GUIs. The evaluation examines functional behavior, visual fidelity, and runtime responses to produce task-specific diagnostic feedback.

name: Reliable Weak-to-Strong Monitoring of LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study also examines tool-calling agents in SHADE-Arena; CUA-SHADE-Arena is its computer-use setting.
summary: Introduces CUA-SHADE-Arena and a red-teaming workflow for testing monitors that detect covert misbehavior in computer-use agent trajectories.

name: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The official full paper confirms GUI/desktop interaction alongside Bash and file tools. Its abstract and body enumerate attack categories differently; no category count is promoted into this annotation.
summary: Introduces AgentSentinel, which intercepts sensitive computer-agent operations and audits them using task context together with system traces. BadComputerUse evaluates this enforcement approach across attack scenarios involving tool and computer control.

name: Detecting Pipeline Failures through Fine-Grained Analysis of Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces a modular framework for identifying errors at intermediate stages of a web-agent pipeline. A SeeAct and Mind2Web case study examines weaknesses that are obscured by final task-success metrics.

name: Robust, Observable, and Evolvable Agentic Systems Engineering: A Principled Framework Validated via the Fairy GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Presents an agent-engineering framework combining runtime goal clarification, an observable component architecture and evolving execution memory. The Fairy mobile GUI agent evaluates these mechanisms on ambiguous tasks and through controlled and user studies.

name: Say One Thing, Do Another? Diagnosing Reasoning-Execution Gaps in VLM-Powered Mobile-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The study measures reasoning and execution gaps across mobile interaction tasks.
summary: Introduces an evaluation framework for mobile GUI agents that compares actions implied by their reasoning with intended and executed actions to diagnose mismatches.

name: GUISpector: An MLLM Agent Framework for Automated Verification of Natural Language Requirements in GUI Prototypes
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The evaluation uses 150 requirements based on 900 acceptance-criteria annotations.
summary: Introduces GUISpector, an MLLM agent framework that operates GUI prototypes to check natural-language requirements and produces feedback for developers.

name: Demystifying deep search: a holistic evaluation with hint-free multi-hop questions and factorised metrics
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The benchmark tests deep search on hint-free multi-hop questions in a controlled Wikipedia sandbox.
summary: Introduces WebDetective, a deep-search benchmark with a traceable Wikipedia sandbox, and EvidenceLoop, an evidence-tracking workflow for web-agent search and synthesis.

name: WebGraphEval: Multi-Turn Trajectory Evaluation for Web Agents using Graph Representation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces WebGraphEval, which merges multiple agents' trajectories into a weighted graph of canonical actions. Structural analyses examine recurring behavior, inefficient paths and important decision points beyond a final success score.

name: GhostEI-Bench: Do Mobile Agents Resilience to Environmental Injection in Dynamic On-Device Environments?
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v3). The attacks are evaluated within Android emulators.
summary: Introduces GhostEI-Bench, a benchmark that injects deceptive UI events into Android emulator workflows to assess mobile agents and analyze failures from actions and screenshots.

name: ProBench: Benchmarking GUI Agents with Accurate Process Information
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: ProBench extends mobile GUI evaluation with tasks whose correctness depends on the interaction process as well as the final state. Its ProcessProvider supplies process information for assessing agent behavior and analyzing failure modes.

name: TaskSense: Cognitive Chain Modeling and Difficulty Estimation for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). Its difficulty estimates are compared with user completion time and agent success on cognitively demanding tasks.
summary: Cognitive Chain estimates GUI task difficulty by extracting sequences of cognitive steps from execution traces, then uses those estimates to assess GUI agents.

name: Computer-Use Agents as Judges for Generative User Interface
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.
summary: AUI-Gym evaluates generated websites by having computer-use agents attempt tasks whose executability is checked programmatically. A feedback dashboard condenses navigation histories into visual summaries that a coding agent can use to revise an interface.

name: MobiBench: Multi-Branch, Modular Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: MobiBench evaluates mobile GUI agents offline while allowing multiple valid action paths. It decomposes agent pipelines into modules to study component contributions, configurations, and performance bottlenecks.

name: A Trajectory-Based Safety Audit of Clawdbot (OpenClaw)
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Audits Clawdbot safety through logged action and tool-call trajectories across local execution and web-mediated workflows, using automated and human review.

name: Web Agents Should Use Typed Actions Instead of Click-Based Browsing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Proposes web verbs as typed actions for web agents, exposing operations with structured inputs, outputs and conditions so agents can compose auditable workflows.

name: CUAAudit: Meta-Evaluation of Vision-Language Models as Auditors of Autonomous Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: CUAAudit examines vision-language models that judge computer-use task completion from an instruction and final environment state. Across macOS, Windows and Linux benchmarks, it measures accuracy, confidence calibration and disagreement between auditors.

name: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent conceptual HCI work about agent-facing interfaces; the abstract does not report GUI task experiments or a new evaluated CUA.
summary: This position paper derives interface design principles from terminal-based human-agent collaboration: representational compatibility, transparent actions and low participation barriers. It argues that graphical and other agent-facing modalities should provide these properties explicitly.

name: AI Planning Framework for LLM-Based Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces a planning taxonomy and trajectory-quality metrics for web agents, supported by 794 human-labeled WebArena trajectories and a comparison of two planning styles.

name: Why Do LLM-based Web Agents Fail? A Hierarchical Planning Perspective
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents a hierarchical planning framework for evaluating web agents at planning, execution and replanning stages, and reports low-level execution as the main failure source.

name: "What Did It Actually Do?": Understanding Risk Awareness and Traceability for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Presents an interview study of computer-use agent risks and AgentTrace, a prototype interface showing agent actions, resource access, permission history, and lasting changes.

name: VenusBench-Mobile: A Challenging and User-Centric Benchmark for Mobile GUI Agents with Capability Diagnostics
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces VenusBench-Mobile, an online benchmark for mobile GUI agents with user-intent-driven tasks and capability annotations for analyzing agent behavior and failures.

name: Same Outcomes, Different Journeys: A Trace-Level Framework for Comparing Human and GUI-Agent Behavior in Production Search Systems
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The framework is instantiated in one audio-streaming search application with 39 participants and ten tasks.
summary: Presents a trace-level framework for comparing GUI agents with people on task outcomes, queries, and interface navigation in a production audio-search application.

name: AgentClick: A Skill-Based Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer for Terminal AI Agents
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent supervision interface: the browser UI is for human review of terminal agents; the abstract does not claim that those agents operate graphical interfaces.
summary: AgentClick gives terminal-based agents a browser review interface for plans, drafts, execution traces and editable memory. A local server and skill plugin let users inspect proposed actions and provide structured feedback.

name: Securing Computer-Use Agents: A Unified Architecture-Lifecycle Framework for Deployment-Grounded Reliability
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Survey of computer-use agent reliability and security across browsers, desktops, and mobile apps, using architecture and lifecycle views to map failures and controls.

name: DiagEval: Trajectory-Conditioned Diagnosis for Reliable Software Evaluation with GUI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: DiagEval diagnoses failed GUI-agent evaluations of interactive software by reusing failed trajectories for targeted probes that distinguish execution errors from defects.

name: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Introduces OpenComputer, which builds desktop tasks around application-state verifiers and refines those verifiers using execution feedback. An evaluation harness records trajectories and assigns auditable partial credit across professional software workflows.

name: AgentHijack: Benchmarking Computer Use Agent Robustness to Common Environment Corruptions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces AgentHijack, a benchmark for desktop computer-use agents facing pop-ups, resolution changes and other common corruptions, alongside an agent that checks its environment.

name: BraveGuard: From Open-World Threats to Safer Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The abstract reports guard evaluation on trajectory-level agent-safety benchmarks.
summary: Introduces BraveGuard, a framework that turns emerging threats and computer-use agent trajectories into training supervision for guards that monitor multi-step safety risks.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.

name: Where Did It Go Wrong? Process-Level Evaluation of Web Agents with Semantic State Tracking
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). Its state tracking relies on websites exposing a deterministic semantic MDP.
summary: Introduces WebStep, a web-agent benchmark that records semantic states behind GUI interactions to analyze exploration, execution accuracy, and decisive errors across task steps.

name: HANSEL: Extracting Breadcrumbs from Web Agent Trajectories for Interactive Verification
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: HANSEL extracts evidence pages and snippets from browser-agent traces and preserves relevant page state in interactive verification views. It flags untraceable answers and evaluates evidence selection and human verification effort separately.

name: When Web Agents Finish but Still Fail: Reproducible Triggers and Trace Diagnostics for Parallel Web Exploration
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2). The benchmark concerns parallel web exploration and answer synthesis.
summary: Introduces Parallel WebBench for parallel web exploration and uses verified URL trajectories to diagnose search loops, incomplete answers, and failures after evidence retrieval.

name: Whose Agent Are You? Multi-Layer Fingerprinting and Attribution of Autonomous Web Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Builds a logging framework that combines network/protocol fingerprints with browser interaction behavior to attribute web-agent traffic. A decision-tree classifier is evaluated across six agent implementations, human browsing and conventional crawlers.

name: Agent MechSuits: Mechanistic Subspace Safety Steering for Multi-Turn CLI Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v2).
summary: Introduces Agent MechSuits, a framework that detects unsafe states and steers multi-turn CLI agents through hidden-representation interventions, alongside the MAS trajectory benchmark.

name: On the Internet, Nobody Knows You're an LLM Bot: Unmasking Web Agents with Multi-Layer Fingerprinting
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Evaluates web agents against anti-bot mechanisms on instrumented honeysites and analyzes network, HTTP and browser fingerprints. The study compares resistance to blocking with the ability to distinguish agents, humans and agent implementations.

name: WebRetriever: A Large-Scale Comprehensive Benchmark for Efficient Web Agent Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: WebRetriever evaluates navigation, knowledge-assisted interaction and end-to-end information-extraction workflows under separate protocols. Its NavEval judge uses richer interaction context to diagnose cases where navigation success does not translate into useful task completion.

name: Tactile: Giving Computer-Using Agents Hands and Feet
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.
summary: Tactile turns accessibility, OCR and visual evidence into explicit desktop targets with executable actions and verification cues. Its execution loop chooses semantic actions or coordinate fallbacks while retaining provenance for replay and diagnosis.

name: Plover: Steering GUI Agents through Plan-Centric Interaction
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Plover exposes GUI-agent plans and replanning as persistent artifacts that users can inspect and edit during execution. Its planner–executor design supports localized correction through plan edits, language guidance and screenshot-grounded interventions, studied through failure repair and workflow scenarios.

name: Just A Rather Very Intelligent Spoken Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces JarvisBench, a benchmark for spoken mediation during long-horizon agent workflows, measuring task collaboration and how users follow ongoing execution.

name: Sidekick: Designing Communication for Effective Multitasking with Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces Sidekick, a communication interface that uses ambient status cues, multimodal action summaries, and visual and verbal explanations of reasoning to help people monitor computer-use agents. A user study examines progress awareness, error traceability, and multitasking across background and foreground interaction.

name: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Audits failure-scored computer-use trajectories to distinguish agent errors from broken tasks and evaluator false negatives. It organizes reliability issues across task construction, trajectory evidence, scoring, and reporting, then derives corresponding evaluation design practices.

name: Software Engineering for and with GUI Agent
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Surveys 336 GUI-agent papers through a software engineering lens, covering architectures, evaluation, and lifecycle concerns in mobile and web settings.

name: ClawProBench: Trace-Aware Evaluation of AI Agents with Runtime Coverage and Frozen Workplace-Style Holdouts
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces ClawProBench, a trace-aware benchmark for agents on OpenClaw that scores workspace and native-runtime tasks using execution traces, safety checks, and process quality.

name: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces CURA, a telemetry-based runtime monitor that turns computer-use trajectories into sequential failure alarms and can trigger mid-task oversight. Its certificate controls false alarms, while the study separately reports detection performance and limits of retrospective monitoring.

name: Monitoring Web Agents Without Internal Signals: Observable Trajectories and Key-Step Supervision
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.
summary: Predicts web-agent failure risk from observable trajectory prefixes using cross-step behavior and black-box consistency queries. Key-step labels preserve valid early prefixes of failed runs, and evaluation tests early intervention and transfer across website categories.

name: OSWorld-Pro: Process-based Evaluation for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Adds annotated intermediate subgoals to computer-use tasks and uses process-oriented evaluation to identify action and progress failures.

name: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Introduces GUITAR, which groups visually different screens into functional states and analyzes agent failures over a state-transition graph. It uses the resulting bottlenecks to diagnose recurring mobile and web errors and evaluate targeted guidance.

name: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Studies repetitive, unproductive actions in desktop agents through their internal activation states. It proposes Reset, Reroute, Restore, a context intervention that temporarily resets an agent’s trajectory and later restores it to help escape repeated ineffective behavior.

name: GUI-HARVEST: Self-Improving GUI Agents through Evidence-Driven Harness Evolution
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Improves GUI-agent execution code by analyzing action effects and repeated-task failures, then validating bounded changes with frozen model weights.

name: Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Audits WebArena-Lite outcomes and trajectories with human review to identify automatic-evaluator false negatives and the first consequential execution errors. It also studies explicit execution-state memory and procedural guidance, showing why final task scores can miss substantial differences in agent behavior.

name: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.
summary: Describes WebFovea, a vision-based live-web agent whose execution loop checks action parsing, browser effects, feedback accuracy, and observation delivery. The report analyzes failures such as coordinate mismatches and silent control interactions and documents corresponding harness changes.

name: AgentTime: Can Agents Estimate and Control Their Own Runtime?
notes: This cross-domain suite includes 16 OSWorld 2.0 tasks among 222 tasks from 18 sources. A single run per task and requested duration, provider effects and incomplete native grades limit comparisons; elapsed time is not evidence of productive work. The OSWorld task 092 video judge was skipped without an API key. The inspected repository README identifies desktop-VM timing and states that the current 222-task forecasting runs will be added; its existing forecasting code covers an earlier study, and transcript work/wait labels are not public. No code or benchmark was executed and no license was verified.
summary: Evaluates duration following, runtime forecasts and elapsed-time estimates in native agent harnesses, including OSWorld desktop tasks, with external timers, native graders and work-versus-wait analysis.

name: Harness Evolution Hits a Ceiling: When Weight Training Should Begin
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The main analysis uses DeepPlanning; WebArena-Lite is a transfer setting.
summary: Studies when to improve an LLM agent's runtime harness or train its weights by classifying failed trajectories; WebArena-Lite supplies a web-task transfer test.

name: From Observations to Authorized Actions: Measuring Source Information in Android Agents
notes: The two prototypes use different workloads and trust assumptions on patched Android/WebView components. Approval is simulated; authenticated browser delivery and atomic capture remain unimplemented. Coarse source history can withhold benign work and persist across tasks. Direct-call checks and limited live-agent trials are separate, and writes are in-memory. No production vulnerability, general defense rate or released artifact is established.
summary: Measures source-attribution limits in Android accessibility and separately tests application-history and selected-WebView-object checks for authorizing AppFunctions actions.

name: MobileJailBench: Red Queen Jailbreak Benchmarking for Mobile Agents
notes: Reviewed the complete retained abstract and selected exact-v1 threat-model, construction and evaluation sections. Execution uses a browser-based Android-like simulator, not real Android isolation or live services. The attacker controls instructions and designated carriers, not privileged simulator state/APIs or system/model/harness internals. Rates depend on release, budget and adjudication coverage. SAF labels track observable expressions and actions, not latent reasoning; unresolved episodes are excluded from rate denominators.
summary: MobileJailBench evaluates mobile-agent jailbreaks in a browser-based Android-like simulator, combining feedback-driven attack evolution, separately admitted task expansions and evidence-grounded outcome adjudication.

name: MobileInject: Evaluating Reasoning-to-Action Security of MLLM-Based Mobile Agents under Cross-Modal Consistency Injection
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 construction, threat-model and evaluation sections. The attacker modifies observation surfaces, not system instructions, model parameters or the OS. State oracles are distinct from emitted-rationale diagnoses, whose labels include outcome-dependent constraints. Those diagnostics are not independent evidence of hidden-reasoning causality.
summary: MobileInject evaluates visual/textual observation injection in stateful Android workflows using resettable emulators, benign/adversarial state oracles and trace-based diagnosis of emitted rationales and actions.

name: Comparing Computer Use Behavior Across Multiple Levels of Abstraction
notes: Reviewed the complete abstract and selected v1 taxonomy, annotation, evaluation and limitations sections. MAP analyzes existing human/agent traces rather than deploying a new acting policy. Annotation and timing coverage depend on the source datasets; manual agreement reflects a particular labeling scheme. Behavioral findings do not establish a privacy guarantee.
summary: MAP annotates computer-use traces at linked operation, function/consequence, method and goal levels, then compares human and agent workflows through sequence, pattern and effort metrics.

name: Who Verifies the Agent's Success Claim? Self-Report Leakage in GUI-Agent Completion Judging
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Studies how GUI agents' success claims affect completion judgments and builds a claim-blind auditor that checks reports against recorded traces.

name: Understanding Tool-Mediated Interaction Failures in Agentic GUI Software: An Empirical Study
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The defect library draws from open-source applications.
summary: Malva catalogs failures that make GUI agents' tool-mediated view diverge from the live interface; MalvaGuard checks related tool contracts before deployment.

name: Build or Adopt? Custom-Built vs. General-Purpose LLM Agent Harnesses for Automotive GUI Testing
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The comparison uses one organization's vehicle test cases, public-app tasks, and practitioner interviews.
summary: Compares a custom harness with general-purpose LLM agent harnesses for GUI testing of Android-based vehicle interfaces and tasks in public apps.

name: When to Intervene? An Empirical Study of Errors and Self-Recovery in LLM Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The recovery predictor is evaluated on ReInBench.
summary: Introduces ReInBench, annotated computer-use and web-agent error traces, and ReCoF, a method for predicting whether an agent will recover without intervention.

name: EnvOS: Auditing Computer-Use Agents When the World Moves On : Phenomenon-Based Task Construction, Certification, and Evidence-Based Evaluation
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The agent studies focus on stale information in clinic booking and insurance-claim approval.
summary: Introduces EnvOS, a framework for constructing and auditing changing computer-use environments, including checks of task changes, solvability, grading, and run evidence.

name: VeriCUA: Verification as Agentic Exploration for Computer-Using Agents
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1).
summary: Introduces VeriCUA, a cross-platform task verifier that gathers evidence through GUI or code checks to assess computer-use agent completion.

name: Interpretable Early Termination of Web Navigation Agents via Closed Sequential Pattern Mining
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained arXiv abstract (v1). The reported evaluation uses 1,544 MiniWoB++ traces from three open-weight language models.
summary: Applies sequential pattern mining to MiniWoB++ web-agent traces, producing reviewable failure signatures and an early-termination policy to reduce token use.

summary: Local, cloud-free replay debugger that records each Browser Use step's screenshot, URL, action and model I/O as a timeline and reports the step at which a failed run diverges from a known-good one.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Two stages per task run: a request interceptor inside the container blocks the final HTTP request and marks the run intercepted when its URL regex and method match the task's eval_schema; an LLM judge (default deepseek-v4-pro at temperature 0) then checks the intercepted body against the instruction. A pass needs both. The original V1 paper rubric instead compares agent and human-reference trajectories.
focus: everyday online tasks on production websites
benchmark_protocol.notes: The README says two ASPCA tasks were removed after publication, so the shipped corpora hold 152 and 129 tasks while scoring.md still divides by 153 and 130. Live sites change over time, and the README asks for comparisons under the same corpus revision, harness and rubric. Agents run through selectable harnesses (for example Hermes and OpenClaw), so observations and actions depend on the harness.

name: ClawBench
notes: Renamed from reacher-z/ClawBench; both API names return repository 1206519531 (TIGER-AI-Lab/ClawBench), which is not a fork and not archived. Counts and scoring rules were read at commit 07eb50a3. The tree also holds v1-lite, claw-eval and environmental-observation task folders, which are not counted here. Task definitions and execution traces are also published as Hugging Face datasets (NAIL-Group/ClawBench, NAIL-Group/ClawBenchV1Trace, TIGER-Lab/ClawBenchV2Trace), whose cards and licenses were not reviewed for this record. Apache-2.0 is recorded for repository code only. Nothing was installed or run.

name: ORBIT framework
notes: BrowserART tools return accessibility trees, including the screenshot-named refresh. Qualification is scenario-specific: the project documents browser-judge and desktop-scoring limits; its opt-in exact-send oracle covers one derived local task, not SMTP delivery. Runtime profiles and scoring policies are separate. Apache-2.0 is the top-level Orbit code declaration; third-party components and external data/environments retain separate terms. No installation, release archive or live evaluation was tested.
summary: Inspect-based multi-agent evaluation framework with role, scheduling and communication controls, BrowserART accessibility-tree actions, and desktop mouse, keyboard and screenshot tools.
